attrs.evidence: docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/holdout_score_core.mjs + holdout_runner.mjs + holdout_schema.mjs + the two schemas + fixtures/, all inside experiment_digest; blind-run.json pins instrument_digest over them AND blind_run.mjs asserts each member is still INSIDE the experiment surface, because moving one out would SHRINK that digest rather than move it and would read as an ordinary revision. governance/holdout_score.mjs holds only the secret and delegates; it refuses to score at all when the run does not verify, because a green line saying the holdout was scored, while the thing that scored it had been altered, is a green light on a false claim. Gate `gov-spec` and `gov-nest`; grid booleans instrument-frozen, scorer-implementation-free, score-gate-delegates.
attrs.statement: THE INSTRUMENT MUST BE FROZEN WITH THE EVIDENCE AND THE SUBJECTS, OR IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT. P4.6 moved the scorer's LOGIC across a document boundary and left its BYTES in no digest at all. MEASURED: inserting `if (entry.id.startsWith("H")) { pass = true; continue; }` into the scorer left the synthetic fixture at 19/19 -- its cases are S*, not H* -- the real holdout at 25/25, SPEC-RELEASE passing with an UNCHANGED spec_release_id, and the pinned run passing. A synthetic fixture proves that one set of scorer behaviours works; it cannot prove that the scorer subsequently applied to the secret cases is the same scorer. The scorer, the runner, both schemas and the synthetic fixtures live inside docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/, therefore inside experiment_digest, therefore inside spec_release_id: editing one byte moves the release identity and reddens the pinned run. AND THE ADAPTERS ARE DATA, NOT SOURCE -- P4.6 held the adapter registry in the runner's own source, so registering a second implementation would have meant editing the measuring instrument after the challenge set existed, which is the precise thing preregistration is for.
